differences.what: the stable's place along the yard: through the house's camera the whole stable renders about 145-165 px right of where the photograph shows it (the lantern at x 1755-1845 against the print's 1610-1700, the wall gable at 1865-1945 against 1720-1793, and the storey-and-a-half wing's gable, which the print shows at x 1867-1945, beyond the frame at x 2035+): about 4 m along the wall at this distance. The stable stands where the 1911 sheet draws it; no camera fits the house's corners and the wing's corner both (the solve's search), and the house's own record has the fit and the sheet disagreeing by up to 2.5 m on its bay, so the gap is the sheet's against this camera, unresolved
differences.how: T-3316 (2026-11-03), under T-3153's rule that a gap two camera fits disagree about is within tolerance: the house's own camera (T-3240's four points) puts the sheet's stable about 167 px right of the print's, and a joint fit of those four points with six of the stable's features (the wing's corner, the lantern, the wall gable, three oculi), the focal freed, puts it within 9 px of the print but reads the house's south-west cornice bed at 8.3 m against 10.8 m. The sheet's place stands: moving the stable about 4 m north to suit the house's camera would carry its north wall across the 1701/1637 lot line the sheet draws 0.6 m from it. Registered on the wing's corner (the render shifted 167 px), every feature reads within about 0.5 m of the print's: the lantern about 23 px, the wall gable about 15 px, the wing's gable apex 3 px, its feet and the lunette within 8 px, the oculus 1 px, the low band 2 px.
